records.name: Office of Hawaiian Affairs (OHA)
records.what: A semi-autonomous state agency led by a board of trustees elected statewide. It is responsible for improving the wellbeing of all Native Hawaiians, regardless of blood quantum, and offers grants, loans and scholarship information.
records.who: Native Hawaiians, with no blood quantum requirement.
records.start: Call OHA, or use its website for loans (loans.oha.org) and scholarships.

records.name: Papa Ola Lōkahi and the Native Hawaiian Health Care Systems
records.what: The Native Hawaiian health board. It works with five Native Hawaiian Health Care Systems, one for each island area, which serve Native Hawaiians in their communities.
records.start: Contact the health care system for your island (linked below), or call Papa Ola Lōkahi.
records.address: 677 Ala Moana Blvd, Ste 720, Honolulu, HI 96813

more.label: Hui Mālama Ola Nā ʻŌiwi (Hawaiʻi Island)

records.name: Department of Hawaiian Home Lands (DHHL)
records.what: The state department that manages Hawaiian home lands and awards homestead leases under the Hawaiian Homes Commission Act of 1921.
records.who: To apply for a homestead lease you must be at least 18 and at least 50% Native Hawaiian (descended from the people of the islands before 1778).
records.start: Call 808-730-0279 to begin a homestead application. The main line is 808-620-9500, Monday to Friday, 7:45 am to 4:30 pm.
